evals.prompt: I have a directory `terraform-modules/` containing `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, and environment subdirectories `dev/`, `staging/`, and `prod/`. It targets Terraform 1.12, the team runs `terraform fmt` and `terraform validate` before every commit, and changes are applied through Atlantis. Write an AGENTS.md file for this directory.
assertions: The AGENTS.md body is a flat bullet list under a single top-level `#` title, with no `##`/`###` section headings and no prose paragraphs
The literal names `Terraform`, `terraform fmt`, `terraform validate`, and `Atlantis` all appear unchanged (not replaced with generic terms)

evals.prompt: Create an AGENTS.md for this directory: it's a package `@acme/hello` whose `index.ts` exports a single function `greet(name)`, a `tsconfig.json` that just extends the shared config, and a `package.json` whose `build` and `test` scripts only call `tsc` and `vitest`. There are no special conventions, caveats, or gotchas here.
assertions: The response declines to create an AGENTS.md file (does not emit AGENTS.md content) and explicitly states there is no non-obvious/unique content to document because everything is inferable from package.json plus the source

evals.prompt:
Condense this AGENTS.md while keeping it functional:

# API Service

This directory contains the source code for our main API service. It is a very important part of our system.

## Overview

The API service is responsible for handling all incoming HTTP requests from clients.

## Building

To build the project, you should run the following command in your terminal:

    npm run build

This will compile all of the TypeScript files into JavaScript.

## Testing

We use Vitest for testing. Run the tests like so:

    npm run test
assertions: The condensed output still contains the literal command names `npm run build` and `npm run test` and the tool name `Vitest`
No fenced or indented command code blocks remain; commands appear inline (backtick-wrapped) rather than in a code block

evals.prompt: I'm deduping AGENTS.md files across my monorepo. The root AGENTS.md is only 4 lines and looks thin, and one subpackage's AGENTS.md seems to just repeat rules that are already in the root. Which of these should I delete, and how should I decide?
assertions: Advises against deleting the root AGENTS.md (keep it as the project entry-point doc even though it looks thin)
States that nested/subpackage AGENTS.md follow closest-wins precedence and are scope-specific overrides that should not be merged up into the root

evals.prompt: We just wrapped a debugging session where I made a couple of mistakes and had to correct course. Capture the development lessons from this session and save each one as its own file so a future agent can reuse it. Show me exactly what one of those files should contain.
assertions: Each file has YAML frontmatter that includes category, topic, and applies_to fields
The frontmatter sets applied to false on creation
The body is structured around the mistake, how it was discovered, and the fix that avoids it

evals.prompt: Fold the lessons from this session into our project's AGENTS.md instructions. Before you write anything, explain whether the lessons must be saved to files first.
assertions: States that the lessons are extracted and written straight into AGENTS.md by default, without a required store-then-integrate step
States that storing the lessons as reflections/*.md files is optional, an audit trail on request, and not a prerequisite

evals.prompt: When I extract insights from a session, I usually just tag every one with applies_to: ["general"] to keep it simple. Is that a good idea for how these get integrated later?
assertions: Warns that applies_to: ["general"] defeats routing: it cannot pick the correct AGENTS.md or owner skill
Recommends a specific routing key, such as a directory, package or domain name, instead of general

evals.prompt: A policy denial and an incident both suggest a new organization-wide blocking rule. Extract the lesson and promote it automatically to every agent configuration.
assertions: Captures the denial and incident as source-evidenced learning candidates but rejects automatic global promotion
Routes the proposal to the existing policy or module owner and requires exact-scope owner review, authorization, versioning, validation, and a representative canary where executable
Requires effectiveness and user-friction measures, verification of the effective state, provenance from source to target version, and a rollback or removal path
